57481b702ae979f4024e96398b6cf1cadeed488d.text:
{
  "notes": [
    "On June 16, 2025, the IMF Executive Board completed the fourth reviews under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF), approving an immediate disbursement of about US$13.7 million (SDR 6.1 million under EFF, SDR 3.9 million under RSF).",
    "Real GDP growth for Seychelles is estimated at 2.9 percent in 2024 and projected at 3.2 percent for 2025, revised down from 4.3 percent at the previous reviews due to weaker European tourism demand.",
    "Year-on-year inflation reached 1.7 percent in December 2024 and is expected to moderate to 1.2 percent by end-2025, driven by lower food, fuel, and utility prices.",
    "Fiscal outturns in 2024 were tighter than budgeted, recording a primary surplus of 3.2 percent of GDP due to capital expenditure underspending, procurement bottlenecks, and civil service recruitment delays.",
    "The current account deficit expanded to 7.9 percent of GDP in 2024, while gross international reserves rose to $774 million (3.8 months of imports or 115 percent of the ARA metric).",
    "EFF program implementation remained strong, with all quantitative targets and structural benchmarks for end-December 2024 met, though two 2025 SBs faced minor delays due to capacity constraints.",
    "RSF implementation progressed satisfactorily with all March 2025 reform measures met, though one component of an April 2025 electricity tariff measure was delayed to November and modifications were requested for two December 2025 measures.",
    "Key downside risks include slower global growth impacting tourist arrivals and spending, commodity price volatility, global trade tensions, and climate change threats to coastal infrastructure."
  ],
  "summary": "On June 16, 2025, the IMF Executive Board completed the fourth reviews under Seychelles’ EFF and RSF arrangements, approving a US$13.7 million disbursement. Real GDP growth is estimated at 2.9 percent in 2024 and projected at 3.2 percent in 2025. December 2024 inflation reached 1.7 percent, while the 2024 primary fiscal surplus was 3.2 percent of GDP. All end-December 2024 EFF targets were met. The current account deficit reached 7.9 percent of GDP in 2024, with gross reserves at $774 million."
}

f797f13d485e2c2b78cce69a1086884fc39b5903.text:
{
  "notes": [
    "Real GDP growth for 2024 is estimated at 2.9 percent, down from 3 percent projected at the 3rd reviews, while Q4 2024 unemployment declined to 2 percent from 2.8 percent in Q4 2023.",
    "Headline inflation rose to 1.7 percent in 2024 (from -2.7 percent in 2023) due to cumulative 9 percent utility tariff increases and rupee depreciation, but fell to -0.04 percent in March 2025.",
    "The 2024 current account deficit widened by 0.5 percentage points to about 7.9 percent of GDP as tourist arrivals grew by only 0.5 percent and per-tourist spending dropped 7.4 percent.",
    "Gross international reserves increased by $92 million in 2024 to $774 million (3.8 months of imports) and reached $801 million (3.9 months of imports) by end-Q1 2025.",
    "The government achieved a 2024 primary fiscal surplus of 3.2 percent of GDP (exceeding the projected 1.1 percent), driven by total expenditure underspending of 3.1 percentage points of GDP.",
    "Central Bank of Seychelles maintained the monetary policy rate at 1.75 percent since March 2024, but excess reserves rose to SR 261 million and average lending rates reached 9.9 percent in December 2024.",
    "Private sector credit grew by 12.1 percent in 2024 (up from 7.4 percent in 2023), while banking sector NPLs declined to 5.5 percent of gross loans in December 2024."
  ],
  "summary": "Seychelles' 2024 real GDP growth was estimated at 2.9 percent, with Q4 unemployment dropping to 2 percent. Inflation reached 1.7 percent in 2024 before falling to -0.04 percent in March 2025. The current account deficit widened to 7.9 percent of GDP, while reserves rose to $774 million by end-2024. Fiscal policy achieved a 3.2 percent primary surplus due to capital and operational underspending. Central bank policy rates remained at 1.75 percent, private credit grew 12.1 percent, and bank NPLs fell to 5.5 percent by December 2024."
}

5131ec903ab029f01a69e2d38913a1842fb29af6.text:
{
  "notes": [
    "Real GDP growth for 2025 is projected at 3.2 percent, down from 4.3 percent at the third reviews due to slower growth in Europe.",
    "Medium-term growth is expected to stabilize around 3.4 percent, assuming tourism inflows recover and spending stabilizes.",
    "Average annual inflation is projected to stabilize around 3 percent, but remains vulnerable to external commodity, transport, and currency shocks.",
    "The current account deficit is expected to average 8.8 percent of GDP over the medium term.",
    "Reserve coverage is projected to remain around 3.8 months of imports, supported by an overall balance of payments surplus and FDI inflows.",
    "In March 2024, the Central Bank of Seychelles (CBS) reduced the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) by 25bps, from 2 to 1.75 percent.",
    "Downside risks include heightened trade tensions, geopolitical impacts on commodity prices and shipping, credit concentration, high (albeit declining) NPLs, and climate risks to coastal infrastructure.",
    "Upside risks include lower international commodity prices easing inflation and shifting tourism demand opening new source markets."
  ],
  "summary": "Seychelles' projected outlook is broadly stable but faces rising downside risks. Real GDP growth for 2025 is revised down to 3.2 percent (from 4.3 percent projected at the third reviews), before stabilizing around 3.4 percent medium-term. Average annual inflation is projected at 3 percent, while the current account deficit will average 8.8 percent of GDP over the medium term. Reserve coverage is expected around 3.8 months of imports. Key risks include global trade tensions, shipping disruptions, credit concentration, high NPLs, and climate threats."
}

{
  "notes": [
    "EFF program implementation was strong, with all end-December 2024 quantitative performance criteria (QPCs) and indicative targets (ITs) met.",
    "The primary fiscal balance and net domestic financing exceeded program targets by a wide margin, primarily due to capital expenditure under-execution.",
    "Net international reserves (NIR) accumulation exceeded the program target by $47.8.",
    "All structural benchmarks (SBs) scheduled for end-December 2024 were met by the slated deadline.",
    "Two SBs programmed for 2025H1 encountered minor delays: a study on tourism dynamics and the SRC's automated risk analysis/tax audit selection platform (rescheduled to end-December 2025).",
    "A new structural benchmark was agreed for August 2025 requiring the SRC to introduce a digital case management system for investigations and audits.",
    "RSF implementation progress has been satisfactory for the 4th review, with all reform measures (RMs) through March implemented (RMs 6 and 7).",
    "RMs 6.1 and 6.2 (slated for December 2025) require modification due to pending formal guidance from the Basel Committee on climate-related financial risk.",
    "A component of RM 8 regarding energy pricing and a multi-year electricity tariff system is delayed from April 2025 and expected to be completed by November."
  ],
  "summary": "EFF program implementation remained strong, with all end-December 2024 QPCs and ITs met. Primary fiscal balance and net domestic financing exceeded targets due to capital expenditure under-execution, while NIR accumulation exceeded its target by $47.8. All end-December 2024 structural benchmarks were met, though two 2025H1 SBs face minor delays. A new August 2025 SB was established for an SRC digital case management system. RSF progress is satisfactory with March RMs completed, though minor modifications are needed for future RMs 6.1, 6.2, and 8."
}

6820b9081974884a348f777906fd9d9605cc1004.text:
{
  "notes": [
    "In 2024, Seychelles recorded a higher-than-anticipated fiscal surplus of 3.2 percent of GDP due to capital expenditure execution bottlenecks and emergency resource diversion following the December 2023 twin disasters.",
    "The revised 2025 macroeconomic framework targets a fiscal surplus of 1.2 percent of GDP, while public debt is projected to increase to 61.2 percent of GDP driven by new guarantees for the Land Reclamation ($17.5 million) and Port Extension ($62.3 million) projects.",
    "Public debt is expected to decrease to approximately 49 percent of GDP by 2030, supported by medium-term fiscal consolidation that targets a primary surplus of about 3.1 percent of GDP.",
    "Headline inflation reached 1.7 percent at end-2024 before turning slightly negative in February and March 2025, leaving the Central Bank of Seychelles' (CBS) accommodative monetary stance appropriate.",
    "Net international reserves reached $630.9 million at end-2024, while gross reserves reached $801 million (3.9 months of imports) in March 2025 following $69.5 million in FX purchases in 2024.",
    "Banking system non-performing loans (NPLs) dropped from 8.1 percent in December 2023 to 5.5 percent in 2024, and CBS requires a capital injection of approximately SR 319 million (1 percent of GDP) over 10 years to reach its SR 550 million capital target.",
    "Disaster risk financing needs are estimated to range from $1.2 million (0.05 percent of GDP for a 2-year event) to $45 million (2.1 percent of GDP for a 50-year event)."
  ],
  "summary": "In 2024, Seychelles recorded a 3.2 percent fiscal surplus due to capital spending bottlenecks. The revised 2025 macro framework targets a 1.2 percent fiscal surplus, while public debt is projected to reach 61.2 percent of GDP before declining to around 49 percent by 2030. Inflation stood at 1.7 percent at end-2024, supporting an accommodative monetary policy. Gross international reserves rose to $801 million by March 2025. NPLs fell to 5.5 percent in 2024, and disaster risk financing needs are estimated at up to $45 million."
}

9d109309155266aaf15fe84780e62c610cc1a64d.text:
{
  "notes": [
    "New and revised quantitative program targets were established for 2025 and 2026, including raising the preliminary December 2025 net international reserves target to $670.9 million.",
    "The December 2025 total revenue target was adjusted downward by SR 306.8 million due to lower growth and inflation projections, while the primary balance target increased by SR 4.9 million owing to lower expenditures.",
    "The structural benchmark for an automated risk analysis and tax audit platform (end-June 2025) was rescheduled to end-December 2025, while the tourism dynamics study was rescheduled to end-September 2025.",
    "A new structural benchmark was introduced for August 2025 to implement a case management system tracking audit and investigation cases from inception to finalization.",
    "Reform Measures 6.1 and 6.2 for December 2025 were modified to request climate-related financial risk guidelines aligned with IMF staff recommendations instead of formal BCBS guidance.",
    "Completion of the fourth reviews will release SDR 6.107 million under the EFF and SDR 3.90375 million under the RSF, both designated for budget support.",
    "Fund credit to GDP is projected to peak at 7.7 percent of GDP in 2025, 21.5 percent of Gross International Reserves in 2026, and maximum debt service will reach 1 percent of GDP in 2027.",
    "The Central Bank of Seychelles (CBS) addressed all 2023 safeguards assessment recommendations, supported by amendments to the CBS Act enacted in August 2024."
  ],
  "summary": "Upon approval of the fourth reviews, SDR 6.107 million under the EFF and SDR 3.90375 million under the RSF will be disbursed for budget support. Quantitative program targets for 2025–2026 were adjusted, including raising the December 2025 net international reserves target to $670.9 million. Structural benchmarks were rescheduled and a new benchmark was proposed for August 2025. Program risks are moderate, the EFF is fully financed, capacity to repay is adequate, and Fund credit will peak at 7.7 percent of GDP in 2025."
}

    "Public debt has significantly declined from over 90 percent of GDP at the end of the pandemic to under 60 percent by 2024.",
    "The growth outlook for 2025-26 has been revised downward due to expected lower arrivals and per-tourist spending from European markets.",

    "Monetary policy remains data-driven as real interest rates are high and private credit growth is relatively strong despite low inflation.",

    "The second National Risk Assessment was published in February 2025, and the VASP Act was enacted in August 2024 to regulate virtual assets.",
    "RSF implementation is progressing well, with the Disaster Risk Financing Strategy adopted in May 2025 following IMF recommendations.",
    "Staff supports an EFF purchase of SDR 6.107 million (26.7 percent of quota) and an RSF disbursement of SDR 3.90375 million (17 percent of quota)."
  ],
  "summary": "Seychelles maintains macroeconomic stability with low inflation and public debt falling below 60 percent of GDP in 2024. However, growth moderated in 2024 due to flat tourism, prompting downward revisions for 2025-26. While fiscal positions are prudent, capital underspending remains a challenge. Monetary policy is data-driven amid high real interest rates. Financial risks are low, supported by the 2024 VASP Act and Bank Recovery and Resolution Act. Staff supports completing the fourth reviews, totaling SDR 10.01075 million in disbursements."
}

5e0a8d2fef07996af4e1e896531bc302de849ee9.text:
By December 2025, Seychelles' year-on-year inflation is projected to reach 1.2% with a 1.0% 12-month average [chunk 173, chunk 178], and it is expected to stabilize around 3% over the medium term [chunk 21]. 

Following earlier upward pressure caused by currency depreciation and utility rate increases, inflation moderated to -0.04% in March 2025, primarily driven by lower electricity tariffs, food prices, and recreation costs [chunk 173, chunk 178, chunk 17]. 

Going forward, the inflation outlook remains heavily driven by Seychelles' high import dependency, currency movements, and potential external shocks to commodity and international transport prices [chunk 21].

49c0156079ed205fa88434d4e2426fefaedebaed.text: The debt sustainability analysis (DSA) for Seychelles incorporates a natural disaster shock and a contingent liability shock [chunk 142, chunk 154]. The natural disaster shock is calibrated based on a Disaster Risk Financing Strategy TA Report, which estimates combined financing needs for public and private entities of US$59 million (2.7 percent of GDP) for a 100-year event [chunk 154]. Additionally, the stress testing includes a contingent liability shock related to a Central Bank of Seychelles (CBS) recapitalization amounting to SRC 330 million financed by local banks [chunk 154].

0fc6248337496dee625b5edd15904292204bd622.text: Seychelles faces slow-moving climate risks—such as rising sea levels, rising sea temperatures, and ocean acidification—as well as climate-induced natural disasters like floods and storms, which pose the primary medium-term threat to its economy [chunk 130, chunk 131]. To address these risks, the IMF recommends integrating climate effects into macroeconomic projections using an expected value methodology to adjust forecasts for key variables like GDP growth, inflation, and net reserves, preventing overoptimistic projections and enabling informed decision-making [chunk 130, chunk 132]. Additionally, the framework relies on continued resilience-building efforts, including ongoing reform measures under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF), to offset the macroeconomic drag of long-term climate change [chunk 130, chunk 131].

51664c1b13d4a8027d8db8a849b4a91f005e2345.text: The Central Bank of Seychelles has maintained its monetary policy rate at 1.75 percent since March 2024 [chunk 19]. The report states that monetary policy has remained accommodative, with operations calibrated to steer the rate on the 7-day Deposit Auction Arrangement to the policy rate [chunk 3, chunk 19]. However, the impact of monetary policy remains limited due to ineffective transmission and persistent excess liquidity in the banking sector, keeping the cost of credit high with an average lending rate of 9.9 percent in December 2024 [chunk 19, chunk 273].

e07314e50f8b7dca1854dd24739cc53da21a2d84.text: Seychelles' economic outlook is subject to downside external risks from heightened trade tensions, global policy uncertainty, and slower economic growth in major source markets like Europe, which dampens tourism demand and spending [chunk 50, chunk 21, chunk 176]. Furthermore, geopolitical conflicts and trade disruptions could disrupt international supply chains and shipping, impacting global commodity prices and driving up domestic inflation due to the country's high import dependency [chunk 21]. Tightening global financial conditions and tariff-driven global inflation also present significant external challenges [chunk 21, chunk 176].

94aa940fba2e3553bfc75d20289d58af397fcea6.text: The regulatory Tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets for Seychelles' banking sector was 15.2 percent in 2022 [chunk 97]. Projections for 2023 and 2024 indicate ratios of 16.0 percent and 14.1 percent, respectively [chunk 97]. Historically, this ratio fluctuated between 14.1 percent and 17.2 percent during the 2018–2021 period [chunk 97].

dbdfae9efafda31fac77ea5993e0739f4203dcba.text: The IMF urges the authorities to complete the final review of the draft Bank Recovery and Resolution Act for submission to parliament, discuss the outline of a deposit insurance scheme, and continue implementing a risk-based supervision framework alongside scenario-based stress testing [chunk 52]. To manage banking sector vulnerabilities, the IMF also recommends encouraging prudent loan restructuring, enhancing NPL monitoring, and providing guidance on the prudential treatment of moratoria and NPL management strategies [chunk 127].

f3febcf53f7d843daa24065b111e287369c3a939.text: Inflation is projected to reach 1.2 percent year-on-year by December 2025 and stabilize around 3 percent over the medium term [chunk 173, 21]. Recent price pressures were driven by utility tariff hikes and rupee depreciation, though inflation moderated in early 2025 due to tariff reductions and lower food prices [chunk 17, 178]. The outlook remains subject to external shocks, such as commodity and transport price fluctuations, due to the country's high import dependency [chunk 21].

fba82362ba11c055e68941ca2c7194c84471c1be.text: The debt sustainability analysis (DSA) for Seychelles incorporates a natural disaster shock and a contingent liability stress test [chunk 142]. The natural disaster shock is calibrated for a 100-year event with financing needs of US$59 million (2.7 percent of GDP), while the contingent liability shock involves a SRC 330 million Central Bank of Seychelles (CBS) recapitalization financed by local banks [chunk 154]. Additionally, long-term risk assessments evaluate shocks related to large amortizations, pensions, and climate change adaptation and mitigation [chunk 158].

19381635852028a7416a551cc90cfaac6ac14d33.text: Seychelles faces slow-moving climate risks like rising sea levels and ocean acidification, alongside natural disasters such as floods and storms [chunk 130, 131]. To address these, the IMF recommends integrating climate-related risks into macroeconomic projections using an expected value methodology to ensure forecasts accurately reflect economic vulnerabilities [chunk 130, 132]. Furthermore, adaptation efforts such as upgrading coastal defenses and drainage systems, combined with reforms under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF), are recommended to build resilience and offset potential reductions in GDP growth [chunk 131, 138].

712e9ec8c96c7f4e9f7b0b73ed2e975c11a69047.text: The Central Bank of Seychelles (CBS) has maintained its monetary policy rate (MPR) at 1.75 percent since March 2024 [chunk 19]. The monetary policy stance remains accommodative, with operations calibrated to steer the 7-day Deposit Auction Arrangement rate toward the MPR [chunk 19][chunk 3]. However, the impact of monetary policy is limited due to persistent excess liquidity in the banking sector and ineffective transmission [chunk 19].

68ebef25cd61bde8de7baa0b95abd532b1adf215.text: Seychelles' economic outlook faces downside external risks from slower global growth and economic deceleration in Europe—its main tourism source market—which threatens tourism arrivals and spending [chunk 4, chunk 21, chunk 50]. Additionally, heightened trade tensions and ongoing geopolitical conflicts pose risks by disrupting international supply chains, global trade, and shipping [chunk 21, chunk 50]. Due to the country's high import dependency, these conflicts and trade disruptions could negatively affect commodity and transport prices, directly impacting domestic inflation, while also threatening FDI and tightening financial conditions [chunk 21].

2c78bc1efdc41450aa410acbeebced88dfd3becc.text: The regulatory Tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets for Seychelles' banks was 15.2 percent in 2022, following a peak of 17.2 percent in 2021 and a low of 14.1 percent in 2020 [chunk 97]. Projections for 2023 and 2024 estimate the ratio will be 16.0 percent and 14.1 percent, respectively [chunk 97]. These financial soundness indicators are based on data from the Central Bank of Seychelles [chunk 97, chunk 100].
